title: Real-time updates: polling, SSE, WebSockets, push
summary: Pick the channel by direction, frequency and app state: polling for rare updates, SSE for server-to-client streams, WebSockets for bidirectional low latency while foregrounded, APNs when the app is backgrounded.
requirements: Latency target (sub-second chat vs minutes for a feed badge).
Behavior in background and on flaky networks; battery cost.
components: APNs (alert or silent) to wake or notify when not connected
tradeoffs: Polling is simple and cache-friendly but wastes requests and adds latency.
WebSockets give the lowest latency but need stateful servers, sticky routing, and are dropped when the app is suspended.
Push works in background but is best-effort, throttled (silent pushes) and limited in payload (4KB).
HTTP/2/3 streams reduce the cost of many small requests, narrowing the gap with sockets.
body: **Typical hybrid (chat):** WebSocket while foregrounded; on disconnect, fall back to push for new-message alerts; on reconnect or foreground, sync missed messages via REST using the last received sequence number. The socket is an optimization; REST sync is the source of truth.
**Reconnect:** exponential backoff with jitter, reset on success; react to `NWPathMonitor` changes; heartbeat (ping) every 20-30s to detect dead connections behind NATs.
**Ordering and dedupe:** server-assigned sequence numbers per conversation/channel; client tracks the highest contiguous sequence and requests gaps.
**Battery:** close the socket when backgrounded; batch updates; avoid waking the radio for low-priority data.
